basics.name: Taha Shaheen
basics.summary:
Teaching robots to collaborate with and adapt to imperfect human partners.

I am a Computer Science Ph.D. student at Arizona State University investigating how a mismatch between a human's understanding of domain dynamics affects the quality of their feedback, and how this in turn impacts an agent's reward learning.

My background includes the identification and prevention of misuse of teleoperated robots at Kyoto University, and engineering low-cost socially assistive robots for autism therapy at NED University of Engineering and Technology.

Seeking a full-time, 12-week internship for Summer 2026.

work.name: Cooperative Robotic Systems Lab, Arizona State University
highlights: Engineered a full-stack data collection platform (Python, Flask, JS) for a large-scale HRI study, successfully collecting over 2,550 unique trajectories from 140+ participants in a custom grid-world environment.

Designed and executing a 16-condition study, examining the impact of perturbed user beliefs on feedback quality in reward learning for robots, in collaboration with ASU's most-cited researcher, Dr. Stephen G. West.
Accelerated the development cycle by an estimated 30-40% through AI-assisted rapid prototyping and deployed an automated pipeline for data collection and processing, minimizing manual intervention.

work.name: School of Computing and Augmented Intelligence, ASU
work.summary: Courses including Mobile Computing (CSE 535), Information Assurance (CSE 543), Assembly Language (CSE 230), and 486 (Capstone). Delivered lectures, designed projects, hosted office hours, and assisted students with course material.
highlights: Teaching Excellence Award (2025)

work.name: Human-Robot Interaction Lab, Kyoto University
highlights: Devised a novel role-playing study to explore adversarial behaviors yielding key insights for future robotic ethics frameworks where 12 participants used both a physical robot and a crowded simulation to act as malicious operators and victims.
Identified and cataloged 15 unique “low-moral” actions (e.g., privacy violation, harassment), and developed a framework of technical and social countermeasures to prevent them.
Authored the resulting taxonomy and prevention framework, culminating in a first-author publication in the journal ACM Transactions on Human-Robot Interaction.

work.name: National Center for Artificial Intelligence, NED University
highlights: Engineered 2 socially assistive robots from concept to deployment for a target cost under $200 USD, developing the full software/hardware stack in Unity (C#), Android (Java), and Arduino (C++).
Drove 3 major robot iterations by incorporating insights from a 3-month field study and targeted feedback from 15 key stakeholders (therapists and parents).
Mentored 12 undergraduate students across 3 capstone teams on robotics projects for autism therapy, leading all 3 teams to successfully develop and validate novel therapeutic robot prototypes.

work.name: Fatima Fertilizer Company
work.position: Graduate Trainee Engineer, Instrumentation and Control
highlights: Managed day-to-day maintenance jobs at Offsites & Utilities and Nitric Acid plants.
Completed training in field instrumentation, Bently Nevada vibration monitoring, anti-surge control, DCS/ESD systems, and process safety management.
Supervised the training of interns and junior trainee engineers.

projects.name: Active Shadowing (ASD) for Implicit HRI Communication
highlights: Contributed to the development of Active Shadowing, a novel system using Augmented Reality shadows to enhance robot collaboration without sacrificing motion optimality.
Developed the core robot control software, precisely choreographing a UR5 arm's movements to seamlessly integrate with a predictive Augmented Reality shadow projected via a HoloLens.
Co-designed the 23-participant user study that validated the system, proving via t-test (p<0.05) that the AR shadow improved human-robot safety scores by over 50% compared to explicit communication.

projects.name: LLM as a Model Optimizer in Model Predictive Control
highlights: Proved that an LLM can function as a real-time model optimizer for an MPC system, successfully adapting the controller parameters online to stabilize a dynamic inverted pendulum simulation.
Engineered a physical testbed for hardware validation by designing and 3D-printing a custom pendulum and integrating it with a UR5 robotic arm.

projects.name: Office Reception Robot
highlights: Engineered the robot's perception and interaction systems, integrating a Python-based computer vision module for facial recognition and Google Dialogflow for natural language understanding (NLU).

Built the full-stack architecture, including a Python back-end and 3 custom Android front-ends, to successfully automate 3 core office tasks (guest registration, package delivery, and meeting scheduling).

projects.name: Assistive Social Robot (Capstone Project)
highlights: Designed, built, and deployed a social robot from the ground up, developing the full stack using Unity (C#), Android (Java), and Arduino (C++).

The project's success and technical novelty directly led to securing a $26,000 grant from Pakistan's Higher Education Commission (TDF-02145), which funded its continuation as a formal research position.

volunteer.organization: School of Computing and Augmented Intelligence (SCAI), ASU
volunteer.summary: Collaborated with the Communications Specialist to co-manage the SCAI PhD Post, a monthly newsletter featuring the key updates and achievements of the PhD students at SCAI.

Guided Japanese high school students through tours in Kyoto, interacting in English to increase their confidence in speaking a foreign language. Introduced students and cafe patrons to Pakistani culture through presentations and conversations.

volunteer.organization: 1947 Partition Archive and Stanford University Libraries
volunteer.summary: Supervised and assisted three volunteers in rural Sindh and Karachi in recording and preserving the life stories and oral histories of witnesses of the 1947 Partition of British India. Collectively recorded 90 stories.

Located and interviewed 83 witnesses of the 1947 Partition of British India to preserve their life stories and oral histories. Organized two events called Voices of Partition where witnesses and survivors of the 1947 Partition told their stories.
highlights: Interviewed by BBC Radio for my volunteer work. The documentary can be found at: https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/p05b70f4
